To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a nucleoprotein antigen was found in mink lung tumor cells transformed by the v-fes oncogene.
the chromatin from two different oncogenically transformed mink lung cell lines, each transformed by a different oncogene, was found to be immunologically indistinguishable.

chromatin prepared from mink lung cell lines transformed by two different oncogenes revealed immunological profiles indistinguishable from one another, but significantly different from chromatin of untransformed parental cells, as determined by the use of cross-tested xenoantisera.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new approach for detecting and identifying tumor-associated antigens, and with the application of this technique to the detection of a tumor-associated antigen in mink cells transformed by two oncogenes.

a new method of detection of tumor-associated nucleoproteins in transformed cell lines, and with the identification of a tumor-associated antigen in mink cells transformed by either the oncogenes of murine sarcoma virus or of avian sarcoma virus.
the detection of a tumor-associated antigen in chromatin from cells transformed with viral oncogenes, and with the possible role of such an antigen in the transformation process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the chromatin from each transformed cell type contained an antigen not present in the chromatin from the parental cell line, and that the chromatin of each transformed line contained a similar antigenic determinant.
the chromatin from the v-mos- and v-fes-transformed cells contain a common tumor-associated antigenic determinant, which is not detectable on the untransformed cell line.
the chromatin from each cell line contains a tumor-associated nucleo- protein antigen which may be the same in both transformed lines and different from the untransforme d parental cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the v-mos and v-fes oncogenes induce similar alterations in mink lung cell chromatin, as revealed by their immunologically similar tumor-associated nucleoproteins.

the antigenic determinants on the nucleoprotein chromatin are different for the transformed and untransformed cells, and that the antigenic profiles for the two different oncogenically transformed cells are similar.
a tumor-associated nucleoantigen is present in mink lung cell lines transformed by either v-fes or v-mos, and that the nucleoprotein antigen is not present in the parental cell type.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oncogenic transformation event in each case resulted in the appearance of a tumor-associated antigen that is not detectable in the untransformed cell line.
chromatin from cells transformed with two different oncogenes (v-fes and v-mos) can induce the production of xenoantisera with immunoreactivity to chromatin from cells containing the other oncogene.
the oncogenicity of a given cell is not reflected in its chromatin structure, as determined by immunological analysis of chromatin antigens.
